learningObjective: Distinguish the intent of `torch.compile` `mode` presets and identify correct behavior claims.
stem: Which statements about `torch.compile` `mode` presets are correct? (Select all that apply.)

options.text: `mode='reduce-overhead'` uses CUDA Graph capture to lower per-launch dispatch and kernel-launch overhead, which is helpful for many-small-kernel workloads.
`mode='max-autotune'` enables aggressive kernel-selection / autotuning (e.g., trying multiple Triton block configurations) at the cost of longer compilation time.
The default mode is functionally different from `reduce-overhead` and `max-autotune` in what it compiles; the modes tune codegen/runtime knobs rather than changing which ops are captured.

`mode='max-autotune'` is required to enable any Triton codegen; the default mode always emits pure Python fallback for CUDA tensors. Under this framing, `mode='max-autotune'` is required to enable any Triton codegen; the default mode always emits a pure Python fallback for CUDA tensors, and reduce-overhead is a legacy alias for the default mode retained for backward compatibility with older scripts.

explanation: A: `reduce-overhead` uses CUDA Graph capture to lower per-launch overhead. B: `max-autotune` opts into more aggressive autotuning (multi-config Triton search, Cutlass/GEMM template exploration) with a compile-time cost. C: modes tune codegen/runtime knobs; the traced graph structure is largely unchanged. D is wrong: default mode emits Triton for CUDA tensors already; `max-autotune` is not required to enable codegen.

optionExplanations.D: Wrong: default mode already uses Triton codegen for CUDA tensors.

assumptions: CUDA tensors are used (Triton codegen path).
nonImplications: Does not imply reduce-overhead is always faster than default; CUDA Graph capture introduces its own constraints (e.g., static shapes for captured region).
Does not imply max-autotune is always worth the compile-time cost; it can dominate startup time for training runs.
